title: Jehu
lead: An army commander anointed king of Israel at Elisha's word, who killed Joram, Ahaziah and Jezebel, wiped out Ahab's family and the worship of Baal, and founded the longest-lasting dynasty of the northern kingdom (about 841–753 BC). Kings praises his zeal; the prophet Hosea condemns his bloodshed.

sections.b: God tells Elijah at Horeb to anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king (1 Kings 19:16–17), but it is a young prophet sent by Elisha who does it (2 Kings 9:1–10). Jehu's revolt fulfills Elijah's word against Ahab's house and Jezebel (1 Kings 21:21–24; 2 Kings 9:36; 2 Kings 10:10, 17). The LORD promises his sons the throne for four generations (2 Kings 10:30), and the narrator notes that this came true (2 Kings 15:12). But Jehu keeps Jeroboam's calves (2 Kings 10:29–31), and Hosea names his son Jezreel because God "will bring the blood shed at Jezreel down on the house of Jehu" (Hosea 1:4). Outside the Bible, Jehu is the only Israelite king pictured in a carving: he or his envoy kneels before Shalmaneser III on the Black Obelisk (841 BC).
